clue.text: Gamble, without question in pursuit of money? That shows guts!

indicators.note: following behind, so the money piece comes first and the rest after it
here in its old sense of outside: the gamble word goes round the question word

explanation.surface: Someone stakes everything on a cash prize without asking, and the onlooker admires their nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking; 'guts' looks like courage but means the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Breadbasket is informal slang for the stomach, and guts likewise names the belly and innards.

clue.text: Attended a music event — loved keeping volume turned up

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the letters read from bottom to top
holding inside, so the volume letter sits within the loved word

explanation.surface: A music fan had a great time at a gig with the volume cranked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping' puts V inside DEAR to give DEVAR; 'turned up' reverses it in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To rave is to go to a rave, a large dance party with loud electronic music.

clue.text: Tree, mostly formal, occupying a bed

indicators.note: taking up space inside, so the shortened formal word sits within the bed phrase

parts.note: a cot is a small bed

indicators.note: most of the word, with its last letter dropped

explanation.surface: A stiff, proper tree seems to have taken over a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of the formal word before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The apricot is a fruit tree bearing small orange stone fruit.

clue.text: Rouse top former tax officials?

parts.note: to top is to beat, or best
IR is the Inland Revenue, the UK tax authority before it merged into HMRC in 2005

explanation.surface: A question whether to stir up the most senior of the old taxmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like an adjective but is the verb to best.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestir oneself is to rouse oneself into action.

clue.text: It's not looking good as an option for union

definitions.meaning: ill health is a state of looking unwell
the marriage vow 'in ... and in health' offers it as one of the conditions of the union

explanation.surface: A cryptic remark that something unattractive could still be chosen in a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: Illness is not looking well, and the wedding vow promises fidelity in it or in health.

clue.text: Energy subordinate to power in revised Green table display

indicators.note: the pair of letters goes inside the rearranged word
altered, so the letters of green are rearranged
in a down clue, below, so the energy letter comes after the power letter

parts.note: P is the symbol for power
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A note on energy policy: power takes precedence in a revised Green manifesto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revised' turns GREEN into ERGNE; PE goes inside after the first E.
explanation.definitionFit: An epergne is an ornamental centrepiece for a dining table, holding fruit or flowers.

clue.text: Boast about ship, remote and insubstantial? It's hardly worth anything

indicators.note: around, so the boast word encloses the rest

explanation.surface: A braggart's ship, far away and flimsy, is hardly worth a thing.
explanation.walkthrough: A farthing was an old British coin worth a quarter of a penny; the phrase is usually 'not a brass farthing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Not a brass farthing is an idiom for nothing at all; the farthing was the smallest coin.

clue.text: Local politician from the South called US city about Republican

indicators.note: in a down clue, read from the bottom upwards
around, so the called word encloses the party letter

explanation.surface: A councillor rings from the South, calling about a Republican in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the South' reverses the whole assembled string, since in a down entry it reads upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An alderman is a member of a local council, a municipal officer.

clue.text: Going off associates in revolutionary movement

parts.note: milk turning is going off, or souring
a circle is a group of friends or associates

explanation.surface: Members leave a radical political movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks political; it is about rotating.
explanation.definitionFit: A turning circle is the smallest circle a vehicle can turn in, a rotating manoeuvre.

clue.text: Club heading off for the Cam?

indicators.note: the first letter is removed

parts.note: a driver is a golf club

explanation.surface: A golf club sets off for Cambridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cam flows through Cambridge; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cam is a waterway in Cambridge, an example of the category.

clue.text: Nice exclamation from unhappy cable user

indicators.note: an unhappy arrangement is a disordered one, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A frustrated cable subscriber lets out a polite cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, not the adjective, so the exclamation is French.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacré bleu is a stereotypical French oath of surprise, heard in a place like Nice.

clue.text: Deceptive activity of the French in part

indicators.note: the French word goes inside the part word

parts.note: du is French for of the

explanation.surface: French involvement in some underhand scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Seduction is luring someone astray, an activity that relies on beguilement.

clue.text: Grassy, about to be covered in dirt?

indicators.note: enclosed by, so the about word goes inside the dirt word

parts.note: gen and dirt are both slang for information

explanation.surface: A lawn so muddy it will soon be covered in dirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dirt' looks like mud but is information, slang GEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Grassy land is verdant, coloured like turf.

clue.text: Somewhat eccentric about key expression of commitment

indicators.note: around, so the eccentric word encloses the key

parts.note: fey means whimsical or a little odd
Alt is a computer keyboard key

explanation.surface: A slightly odd person makes a show of loyalty to a key cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Fealty is a vassal's pledge of loyalty to a lord, an avowed allegiance.

clue.text: Precision in account supplied by church office

parts.note: a curacy is the office of a curate

explanation.surface: A parish office supplies an exact set of accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: Accuracy and precision are synonyms for exactness.

clue.text: Carnal activity — various names about that from uncultured guy

indicators.note: around, so the rearranged letters surround the carnal word
in various forms, so the letters of names are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lewd remark about sex with a list of names, from a boorish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges the names; Essex Man is a British stereotype of a brash, materialistic voter from the county east of London.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a caricature of a vulgar, uncultivated Tory voter from southeast England.

clue.text: Start to see gossip providing unwanted attention?

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Is a glance and a chat the beginning of harassment?
explanation.definitionFit: Stalking is persistent pursuit of someone who does not welcome it.

clue.text: Price set after collapse in takings

indicators.note: once fallen apart, the letters of price set are rearranged

explanation.surface: After a price crash, the shop's income is set.
explanation.definitionFit: Receipts are the money taken in by a business, its revenue.

clue.text: This writer subsequently will accept a Conservative being not wholly Right

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, I

indicators.note: takes in, so a and the party letter go inside

explanation.surface: A writer will later take on a Tory who is not entirely right-wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' with its capital looks political; it means correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexact means imprecise, not entirely correct.

clue.text: Health centre to confirm accepting one, not hospital

indicators.note: the hospital letter is removed
taking in, so the numeral letter goes inside

parts.note: to clinch a deal is to confirm it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A health centre confirms it will take one patient, but it is not a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepting' puts I in CLINCH (CLINICH); 'not' drops the H.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinic is a medical centre for outpatients, smaller than a hospital.

clue.text: From which speaker delivers story I missed about bird

indicators.note: left out, so the I is removed

explanation.surface: A speaker tells a story but loses the thread about a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed' drops I from LIE to leave LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lectern is a stand from which a lecturer or reader addresses an audience.

clue.text: Quantity of water power involving river

indicators.note: including, so the river letter goes inside

parts.note: steam is a source of power

explanation.surface: A volume of water drives a steam engine via a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A stream is a flowing body of water, a brook.

clue.text: Rough having to dispose of a farm animal

indicators.note: getting rid of, so the a is removed

explanation.surface: A rough farmer has to get rid of an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Horses are kept on farms as livestock and working animals.

clue.text: Delayed arrival dispersed morale etc

indicators.note: scattered, so the letters of morale etc are rearranged

explanation.surface: A late arrival scatters the team's morale and so on.
explanation.definitionFit: A latecomer is someone who turns up late.

clue.text: Girl in Scotland right to swap litres for gallons

indicators.note: exchange, so one letter replaces another

explanation.surface: A Scottish lass has every right to swap metric for imperial measures.
explanation.definitionFit: Morag is a Scottish girl's name, a form of Sarah.

clue.text: Fruit having city vermin back in square

indicators.note: the city and reversed vermin go inside the square

parts.note: EC is the City of London postcode

indicators.note: turned backwards, so the vermin word is reversed

explanation.surface: A city square has a pest problem around the fruit stall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'square' is the number nine, a perfect square; 'back' reverses the vermin.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectarine is a smooth-skinned variety of peach.

clue.text: Register name entered in scholarship after setback

indicators.note: put inside the reversed word
set backwards, so the scholarship word is reversed

explanation.surface: A student signs up for a scholarship after a setback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after setback' turns LORE into EROL; N goes in after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol is to put one's name on a register for a course.

clue.text: Organise religious figure, chap caught between eras

indicators.note: sitting between the two era words

explanation.surface: Arranging a holy figure and a man trapped between historical periods.
explanation.definitionFit: To stage-manage is to orchestrate events behind the scenes.
